source.title: Some problems and conjectures about L2-invariants

accepted.question_text: Let F be a field with Q ⊆ F ⊆ C, and let G be a group whose finite subgroups have bounded order. If lcm(G) denotes the least common multiple of the orders of the finite subgroups of G, must every finitely presented FG-module M satisfy the integrality condition lcm(G) · dim_{N(G)}(N(G) ⊗_{FG} M) ∈ Z? Equivalently, when G is torsionfree, are the resulting L2-Betti numbers always integers?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.1 (Atiyah Conjecture). Consider a field F with Q ⊆ F ⊆ C. Let G be a group possessing an upper bound on the orders of its finite subgroups. Let lcm(G) be the natural number given by the least common multiple of the orders of its finite subgroups. We say that G satisfies the Atiyah Conjecture with coefficients in F, if for any finitely presented F G-module M the von Neumann dimension satisfies lcm(G) · dimN(G)(N (G) ⊗F G M) ∈ Z.

accepted.question_text: For a group G and a field F with Q ⊆ F ⊆ C that is closed under complex conjugation, let R_FG be the *-regular closure of FG inside the algebra U(G) of affiliated operators. Is the canonical map colim_{H ⊆ G, |H| < ∞} K_0(FH) → K_0(FG) → K_0(R_FG) always surjective?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.9 (Algebraic Atiyah Conjecture). Let G be a group and let F be a field F with Q ⊆ F ⊆ C, which is closed under complex conjugation. Let RF G be the ∗-regular closure of F G in U(G). We say that G satisfies the Algebraic Atiyah Conjecture with coefficients in F if the composite of the canonical maps colimH⊆G,|H|<∞ K0(F H) → K0(F G) → K0(RF G) is surjective.

accepted.question_text: If M is an aspherical closed topological manifold, must its L2-Betti numbers vanish outside the middle dimension, meaning b_n^{(2)}(M̃) = 0 for every n with 2n ≠ dim(M)? In even dimension 2m, must the middle L2-Betti number satisfy (-1)^m χ(M) = b_m^{(2)}(M̃) ≥ 0, and if M is a closed connected smooth 2m-manifold carrying a negatively curved Riemannian metric, must one even have (-1)^m χ(M) = b_m^{(2)}(M̃) > 0?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.1 (Singer Conjecture). If M is an aspherical closed topological manifold, then we get for n ≥ 0 b(2)n (Mf) = 0 if 2n 6= dim(M). If M is an aspherical closed topological manifold of even dimension 2m , then (−1)m · χ(M) = b(2)m (Mf) ≥ 0. If M is a closed connected smooth manifold of even dimension 2m admitting a Riemannian metric of negative sectional curvature, then (−1)m · χ(M) = b(2)m (Mf) > 0.

accepted.question_text: For a closed smooth manifold M of even dimension 2m, how is the sign of the Euler characteristic constrained by asphericity or sectional curvature? More precisely, if M is aspherical, must (-1)^m χ(M) ≥ 0? If M carries a Riemannian metric, must one have (-1)^m χ(M) > 0 when sec(M) < 0, (-1)^m χ(M) ≥ 0 when sec(M) ≤ 0, χ(M) = 0 when sec(M) = 0, χ(M) ≥ 0 when sec(M) ≥ 0, and χ(M) > 0 when sec(M) > 0?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.2 (Hopf Conjecture). If M is an aspherical closed topological manifold of even dimension dim(M) = 2m, then (−1)m · χ(M) ≥ 0. If M is a closed smooth manifold of even dimension dim(M) = 2m with Riemannian metric and with sectional curvature sec(M), then (−1)m · χ(M) > 0 if sec(M) < 0; (−1)m · χ(M) ≥ 0 if sec(M) ≤ 0; χ(M) = 0 if sec(M) = 0; χ(M) ≥ 0 if sec(M) ≥ 0; χ(M) > 0 if sec(M) > 0.

accepted.question_text: If M is an aspherical closed topological manifold of odd dimension 2m+1, must M be det-L2-acyclic with L2-torsion satisfying (-1)^m ρ^{(2)}(M̃) ≥ 0? If M is a closed smooth (2m+1)-manifold with a negatively curved Riemannian metric, must one have the strict inequality (-1)^m ρ^{(2)}(M̃) > 0? And if M is aspherical of odd dimension and π_1(M) contains an amenable infinite normal subgroup, must ρ^{(2)}(M̃) vanish?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.3 (Hopf Conjecture for L2-torsion). If M is an aspherical closed topological manifold of odd dimension dim(M) = 2m+ 1, then M is det-L2-acyclic, and its L2-torsion satisfies (−1)m · ρ(2)(Mf) ≥ 0. If M is a closed smooth manifold of odd dimension dim(M) = 2m + 1 with Riemannian metric and with sectional curvature sec(M) < 0, then M is det-L2-acyclic, and its L2-torsion satisfies (−1)m · ρ(2)(Mf) > 0. If M is an aspherical closed topological manifold of odd dimension dim(M) = 2m+1 whose fundamental group contains an amenable infinite normal subgroup, then M is det-L2-acyclic and its L2-torsion satisfies ρ(2)(Mf) = 0.

accepted.question_text: Let G act properly and cocompactly on a contractible topological manifold M without boundary. Must the L2-Betti numbers of M with coefficients in N(G) vanish away from the middle dimension, that is, must b_n^{(2)}(M; N(G)) = 0 for every n with 2n ≠ dim(M)?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.4 (Proper Singer Conjecture). A group G satisfies the proper Singer Conjecture, if for any contractible topological manifold M without boundary on which G acts properly and cocompactly, we have for all n ≥ 0 b(2)n (M; N (G)) = 0 if 2n 6= dim(M).

accepted.question_text: For a group G and any matrix A in M_{r,s}(ZG), is the Fuglede-Kadison determinant of the right-multiplication operator r_A: N(G)^r → N(G)^s always at least 1?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 5.1 (Determinant Conjecture for a group G). For any matrix A ∈ Mr,s(ZG), the Fuglede-Kadison determinant of the N (G)-homomorphism rA : N (G)r → N (G)s given by right multiplication with A satisfies detN(G) (rA) ≥ 1.

accepted.question_text: Let G be a discrete group, let G = G_0 ⊇ G_1 ⊇ G_2 ⊇ ... be a finite-index normal chain with trivial intersection, let p: X̃ → X be a G-covering, and let α be a classical invariant such as the Euler characteristic, signature, Betti numbers over Q or F_p, Reidemeister or Ray-Singer torsion, or logarithmic torsion homology size. Does the normalized sequence α(X[i])/[G:G_i] always converge? If it converges, is the limit independent of the chain {G_i}? If both answers are yes, is the limit always the corresponding L2-analogue α^{(2)}(X; N(G))?

evidence.quote: Problem 6.1 (Approximation Problem). (1) Does the sequence converge? (2) If yes, is the limit independent of the chain {Gi}? (3) If yes, what is the limit? The hope is that the answer to the first two questions is yes and the limit turns out to be an L2-analogue α(2) of α applied to the G-space X, i.e., one can prove an equality of the type lim i→∞ α(X[i])/[G : Gi] = α(2)(X; N (G)).

accepted.question_text: If X is a finite contractible CW-complex and G = G_0 ⊇ G_1 ⊇ G_2 ⊇ ... is a finite-index normal chain with trivial intersection, does the sequence b_n(X[i]; F)/[G:G_i] converge for every field F and every n ≥ 0, and is the limit independent of the chosen chain?

evidence.quote: Question 6.5 (Approximation in prime characteristic). Does the sequence bn(X[i];F )/[G:Gi] converge and is the limit limi→∞ bn(X[i];F )/[G:Gi] independent of the chain {Gi} for all fields F and n ≥ 0, provided that X is finite and X is contractible?

accepted.question_text: Let M be an aspherical closed manifold and let M[i] be the finite covers associated to a finite-index normal chain of π_1(M). Must the normalized logarithmic torsion in homology vanish outside the middle odd degree, meaning lim_{i→∞} ln|tors H_n(M[i]; Z)|/[G:G_i] = 0 for every n with 2n+1 ≠ dim(M)? If dim(M)=2m+1 is odd, must M be det-L2-acyclic and satisfy lim_{i→∞} ln|tors H_m(M[i]; Z)|/[G:G_i] = (-1)^m ρ^{(2)}(M̃)?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 6.8 (Homological torsion growth and L2-torsion). Let M be an aspherical closed manifold. Then we get for any natural number n with 2n + 1 6= dim(M) lim i→∞ ln |tors Hn(M[i]; Z)| / [G : Gi] = 0. If the dimension dim(M) = 2m + 1 is odd, then Mf is det-L2-acyclic and we get lim i→∞ ln |tors Hm(M[i]; Z)| / [G : Gi] = (−1)m · ρ(2)(Mf).

accepted.question_text: Let M be an aspherical closed manifold of odd dimension 2m+1, and let M[i] be the finite covers coming from a finite-index normal chain of π_1(M). Must M be det-L2-acyclic, and must the alternating normalized logarithmic torsion sum over all degrees converge to the L2-torsion according to 2 ∑_{n=0}^{m+1} (-1)^n ln|tors H_n(M[i]; Z)|/[G:G_i] → ρ^{(2)}(M̃)?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 6.11 (Modified Homological torsion growth and L2-torsion). Let M be an aspherical closed manifold of odd dimension dim(M) = 2m + 1. Then M is det-L2-acyclic, the limit ... exists and is given by lim i→∞ 2 Σ_{n=0}^{m+1} (−1)^n · ln |tors Hn(M[i]; Z)| / [G : Gi] = ρ(2)(Mf).

accepted.question_text: For a group G and any normal chain {G_i} with trivial intersection, are the L2-Betti numbers of G approximated by those of the quotients G/G_i? Equivalently, for every matrix A ∈ M_{r,s}(QG), does dim_{N(G)} ker(r_A^{(2)}) equal lim_{i→∞} dim_{N(G/G_i)} ker(r_{A[i]}^{(2)}), and for every finite-type G-CW-complex X, does b_n^{(2)}(X; N(G)) equal lim_{i→∞} b_n^{(2)}(X[i]; N(G/G_i)) for all n ≥ 0?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 7.1 (Approximation Conjecture for L2-Betti numbers). A group G satisfies the Approximation Conjecture for L2-Betti numbers if for any normal chain {Gi} one of the following equivalent conditions holds ... dimN(G)(ker r(2)A) = lim i→∞ dimN(G/Gi)(ker r(2)A[i]); ... Let X be a G-CW-complex of finite type ... we get for n ≥ 0 b(2)n (X; N (G)) = lim i→∞ b(2)n (X[i]; N (G/Gi)).

accepted.question_text: For a group G, a normal chain {G_i} with trivial intersection, and a matrix A ∈ M_{r,s}(QG), does the Fuglede-Kadison determinant over G always equal the limit of the Fuglede-Kadison determinants over the quotients G/G_i, namely det_{N(G)}(r_A^{(2)}) = lim_i det_{N(G/G_i)}(r_{A[i]}^{(2)})?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 7.3 (Approximation Conjecture for Fuglede-Kadison determinants). A group G satisfies the Approximation Conjecture for Fuglede-Kadison determinants if for any normal chain {Gi} and any matrix A ∈ Mr,s(QG) we get for the Fuglede-Kadison determinant detN(G)(r(2)A) = lim i∈I detN(G/Gi)(r(2)A[i]).

accepted.question_text: Let M be a Riemannian manifold without boundary with a proper free cocompact isometric G-action, and let M[i] be the quotients by a normal chain {G_i}. Is the analytic L2-torsion over N(G) always the limit of the analytic L2-torsions over N(G/G_i), that is, does ρ_an^{(2)}(M; N(G)) = lim_i ρ_an^{(2)}(M[i]; N(G/G_i)) hold?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 7.4 (Approximation Conjecture for analytic L2-torsion). A group G satisfies the Approximation Conjecture for analytic L2-torsion if for any normal chain {Gi} and Riemannian manifold M without boundary and with a proper free cocompact isometric G-action ρ(2)an (M; N (G)) = lim i∈I ρ(2)an (M[i]; N (G/Gi)).

accepted.question_text: Under the same setup of a normal chain {G_i} acting on a proper free cocompact Riemannian G-manifold M, is the topological L2-torsion over N(G) always the limit of the topological L2-torsions over the quotients G/G_i?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 7.5 (Approximation Conjecture for topological torsion). A group G satisfies the Approximation Conjecture for topological L2-torsion if for any normal chain {Gi} and Riemannian manifold M without boundary and with a proper free cocompact isometric G-action ρ(2)top(M; N (G)) = lim i→∞ ρtop(M[i]; N (G/GI )).

accepted.question_text: Let M be an aspherical closed orientable manifold of positive dimension whose simplicial volume ||M|| vanishes. Must the universal cover M̃ be of determinant class, and must all L2-Betti numbers b_p^{(2)}(M̃) and the L2-torsion ρ^{(2)}(M̃) vanish?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 8.1 (Simplicial volume and L2-invariants). Let M be an aspherical closed orientable manifold of dimension ≥ 1. Suppose that its simplicial volume ||M|| vanishes. Then Mf is of determinant class and b(2)p (Mf) = 0 for p ≥ 0; ρ(2)(Mf) = 0.

accepted.question_text: If G is an infinite finitely generated residually finite group and G_i is a descending chain of finite-index normal subgroups with trivial intersection, must the first L2-Betti number, the cost, and the rank gradient all coincide, i.e. must b_1^{(2)}(G) = cost(G) - 1 = RG(G; (G_i))?

evidence.quote: Question 9.3 (Rank gradient, cost, and first L2 Betti number). Let G be an infinite finitely generated residually finite group. Let (Gi)i≥0 be a descending chain of normal subgroups of finite index of G with intersection {1}. Do we have b(2)1 (G) = cost(G) − 1 = RG(G; (Gi)i≥0)?

accepted.question_text: If G is a finitely presented infinite residually finite group with a descending finite-index normal chain (G_i) of trivial intersection, and F is any field, must the normalized first Betti numbers satisfy lim_{i→∞} (b_1(G_i; F)-1)/[G:G_i] = b_1^{(2)}(G) - b_0^{(2)}(G) = cost(G) - 1 = RG(G; (G_i))?

evidence.quote: Question 9.4 (Rank gradient, cost, first L2-Betti number, and approximation). Let G be a finitely presented infinite residually finite group. Let (Gi) be a descending chain of normal subgroups of finite index of G with intersection {1}. Let F be any field. Do we have lim i→∞ (b1(Gi; F) − 1)/[G : Gi] = b(2)1 (G) − b(2)0 (G) = cost(G) − 1 = RG(G; (Gi)i≥0)?

accepted.question_text: For a finitely generated group G, is the first L2-Betti number always equal to cost(G) - 1, and is the Fixed Price Conjecture true, meaning that every essentially free probability-measure-preserving action of G on a standard Borel space has cost equal to the cost of G itself?

evidence.quote: Question 9.5. Let G be a finitely generated group. Do we have b(2)1 (G) = cost(G) − 1 and is the Fixed Price Conjecture true? (The Fixed Price Conjecture predicts that the cost of every standard action of G, i.e., an essentially free G-action on a standard Borel space with G-invariant probability measure, is equal to the cost of G.)

accepted.question_text: Let G be a finitely generated non-abelian free group. For an automorphism f of G, is the associated L2-torsion always non-positive? What is the structure of the countable set {ρ^{(2)}(f)} obtained from all automorphisms of G? And for a fixed real number r < 0, are there only finitely many conjugacy classes of fully irreducible automorphisms f with ρ^{(2)}(f) = r?

evidence.quote: Question 9.8. Let G be finitely generated non-abelian free group. (1) Is ρ(2)(f) ≤ 0 for any automorphism f of G; (2) What is the structure of the countable set {ρ(2)(f)}, where f runs through the automorphisms of G? (3) Given a real number r < 0, is the set of conjugacy classes of fully irreducible automorphisms f of G with ρ(2)(f) = r finite?

accepted.question_text: If G and H are admissible groups that are measure equivalent with index I(G,H) > 0, must their L2-torsions be proportional with the same index, namely ρ^{(2)}(G) = I(G,H) · ρ^{(2)}(H)?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 10.2. Let G and H be two admissible groups, which are measure equivalent with index I(G, H) > 0. Then ρ(2)(G) = I(G, H) · ρ(2)(H).

accepted.question_text: If M is an aspherical closed Riemannian manifold and M̃ is its universal cover with the lifted metric, must 0 belong to the spectrum of the minimal closure of the Laplacian on L2 p-forms for at least one degree p ≥ 0?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 11.1 (Zero-in-the-Spectrum Conjecture). Suppose that Mf is the universal covering of the aspherical closed Riemannian manifold M (with the Riemannian metric coming from M). Then for some p ≥ 0 zero is in the spectrum of the minimal closure (∆p)min ... of the Laplacian acting on smooth p-forms on Mf.

accepted.question_text: Can one twist L2-invariants by finite-dimensional representations that are not necessarily unitary in a satisfactory general theory? In particular, does twisting preserve L2-Betti numbers simply by multiplying the untwisted L2-Betti number by the dimension of the representation, and for L2-torsion is the regular Fuglede-Kadison determinant continuous?

evidence.quote: A prominent open problem is whether one can twist L2-invariants with (not necessarily unitary) finite-dimensional representations.
For L2-Betti numbers there is the conjecture that this just boils down to multiplying the untwisted L2-Betti number with the dimension of the representation...
A prominent open problem is whether the regulare Fuglede-Kadison determinant is continuous, see [89, Question 9.11].

accepted.question_text: Is there an F_p-analogue N(G; p) of the group von Neumann algebra for a discrete group G, containing the group ring F_pG and equipped with a dimension function on finitely generated projective N(G; p)-modules that extends to all modules well enough to define characteristic-p L2-Betti numbers? If such an algebra exists, do normalized Betti numbers over F_p along any normal chain converge to the resulting characteristic-p L2-Betti numbers?

evidence.quote: This raises the question whether there is an Fp-analogue of the group von Neumann algebra? In order to treat L2-Betti numbers in prime characteristic, one would hope for the existence of a Fp-algebra N (G; p) which contains the group ring FpG and comes with a dimension function...
The hope is that then the corresponding sequences of normalized Betti numbers with coefficients in Fp converge for any normal chain to the L2-Betti numbers with coefficients in Fp...

accepted.question_text: Can condensed mathematics be used to extend the present formalism of L2-invariants in a way that sheds light on existing open problems, for example by producing analogues of the group von Neumann algebra over F_p? More broadly, can L2-invariants be applied to a wider class of geometric problems arising from condensed mathematics or analytic geometry?

evidence.quote: In the context of L2-invariants, condensed mathematics poses at least two interesting questions. (1) The theory of L2-invariants heavily relies on techniques mixing algebra and topology or functional analysis. Can condensed mathematics help to extend the current formalism of L2-invariants in a way which sheds light on open problems in the area? For example, are there analogues of the group von Neumann algebra of a discrete group over Fp? (2) Can L2-invariants be applied to a wider class of geometric problems coming from condensed mathematics?
